name: LITHUANIA

flag.title: Trispalvė
flag.note: Yellow, green & red — sun, forests, bravery

lead: Lithuania is the biggest of the three Baltic countries. It has thick forests, amber beaches, and a fairy-tale red castle on a lake island. One hill is covered in crosses.
geo: Lithuania is almost flat. Its highest hill is only as tall as a 90-storey building. Half the country is forest. 3,000 lakes and rivers dot the land.
The Curonian Spit is a thin sand ribbon, 98 km long, on the Baltic coast. A calm lagoon lies on one side and huge shifting dunes on the other.
animals: The white stork is Lithuania's national bird. Almost nowhere has more stork nests per square kilometre. Wolves roam the deep forests.
European bison, Europe's heaviest land animals, nearly died out. People brought them back to Lithuania's forests. Beavers have returned too.
culture: Lithuanians love singing and basketball. Every four years, tens of thousands sing together at the Song Festival. The national team has won three Olympic bronze medals.
Up to 80% of the world's amber washes onto Baltic shores. Lithuanians have carved it for 4,000 years. On the shortest night, bonfires light up the Joninės festival.
history: Lithuania was once the biggest country in Europe. In the 14th century, its Grand Duchy stretched almost to the Black Sea. King Mindaugas united the tribes in 1253.
In 1989, two million people held hands in a 675-km chain from Vilnius to Tallinn. In 1990, Lithuania became the first Soviet republic to declare independence.
wows: A granite column marks the centre of Europe, just north of Vilnius.
Soviet bulldozers flattened the Hill of Crosses three times, but Lithuanians rebuilt it.
Linguists use Lithuanian to learn how 3,500-year-old Sanskrit sounded.
In 1992, the Olympic team wore tie-dye shirts paid for by the Grateful Dead.
Lithuania makes over half the world's ultrashort science lasers.
The Curonian Spit's dunes drift up to 10 metres a year.
Vilnius Old Town is one of northern Europe's biggest medieval city centres.

myths.fact: Amber is hardened tree sap, tens of millions of years old. Some pieces trap tiny insects.
Beavers eat bark, leaves, and water plants. They chew wood to build dams, not to eat it.
